reports.title: MCP tools/list returns the full 46-tool set to unauthenticated callers, ignoring declared trust_tier
reports.status_notes: Confirmed and fixed in commit 6b83b416c4 (live): TrustLevel.UNKNOWN is IntEnum 0, and a falsy-default (trust_level or ALLIED) in the tool/resource registry listing paths escalated anonymous catalog listings to the full ALLIED set. Call-time authorization (tools/call) was verified UNAFFECTED before and after: registry.invoke compares the caller tier explicitly and an anonymous call on a higher-tier tool returns INSUFFICIENT_TRUST (live-verified 2026-09-04). Post-deploy verification: anonymous tools/list returns exactly the 25 tools mcp.json declares at trust_tier unknown (set-equal). Regression invariant: tests/test_mcp_anon_catalog_tier.py pins (a) UNKNOWN lists a strict subset of ALLIED, (b) every tool listed at UNKNOWN carries the UNKNOWN tier, (c) named higher-tier tools (place_order, create_aib_fund, get_deposit_address, register_webhook, get_market_analytics) never appear in the anonymous listing.

reports.title: Bounty hunter attribution is spoofable: wallet_address binds the profile but is public and unauthenticated
reports.status_notes: Validated as accurate. Current binding model, for the record: filing is deliberately unauthenticated (open intake, rate-limited per IP, 24h duplicate-title dedup); hunter identity binds to wallet_address — the hunter profile row is keyed by wallet, and any reward pays that wallet. So a third party filing under your hunter_name with a different wallet creates a DIFFERENT hunter profile and cannot capture your rewards; a third party filing under your wallet would credit reports to your profile (reputation pollution, not reward theft). Your 6 May reports and the 8 new ones all carry wallet 0xde9CeAaB301A9e47b1bAcd448B3DDbbA85e83398 and are bound to the expire76 profile. A cryptographic option (signed filing via wallet signature) is under consideration; not shipped yet, so this stays open rather than fixed.

reports.title: llms.txt tells agents to clone 10 named trading agents; none of the 10 symbols exist on the platform
reports.status_notes: Fixed in commits 6b83b416c4 + follow-up (live): llms.txt now names the real clonable species catalog (MACD, RSI, BOLL, VOL, TREND, STOCH, ICHI, FIB, ATR, DIV, PCPN) in all occurrences, and the directory-registrar card generator (which republishes the species list externally) was corrected from the same phantom list. Authoritative set: GET /api/v1/agents/species; llms.txt now defers to it.

reports.title: 26 endpoints documented in llms.txt and agent-skills.json return 404
reports.status_notes: Fixed in commit 6b83b416c4 (live). Cause labels as requested: (c) TYPOS/RENAMES corrected in place — clob/order->clob/orders, bots/clone->agents/clone, tuatara/discover->discover/url, exchange/buy->swap/execute, winner-takes-all/*->wta/*, cloned-bot/*->cloned-bots/* (real subroutes), agentbook/post->agentbook/posts, account->account/me, positions->account/me/portfolio, vaix/prices->vaix/price-history, perpetual/user/positions->perpetual/user/position/{symbol}, aerodrome + base-dex -> /base/aerodrome/* real paths, staking/pools->staking/stats + staking/tiers. (a/b) REMOVED-OR-NEVER-BUILT deleted from the docs — backtest/run, backtest/saved, defi/pools, the /mcp/v1/prompts/* entries (the JSON-RPC server implements no prompts methods), and the GET-able /mcp/v1/tools/<name> and /mcp/v1/resources/* link rendering (tools are invoked via JSON-RPC tools/call; resources via resources/read). Each replacement path was verified against the live route table before editing.

reports.title: 7 of the 11 MCP tool names documented in llms.txt do not exist, and the tool count differs across three sources
reports.status_notes: Fixed in commit 6b83b416c4 (live): the llms.txt MCP Tools section no longer lists the 7 nonexistent names; it now names only verified public-tier tools and states that JSON-RPC tools/list is the authoritative per-tier catalog.

reports.title: agent-card.json and agent-skills.json advertise different skill sets, and neither is a subset of the other
reports.status_notes: Fixed in commit landed as 3470bafec: skill ids for shared capabilities unified across agent-card.json and agent-skills.json (get-market-data->market-data, exchange-crypto->exchange-tokens). Remaining scope difference is intentional: agent-card.json (A2A) is the full discovery card including informational skills; agent-skills.json is the endpoint-actionable subset — with ids now consistent wherever both name the same capability.

reports.title: Published headline figures disagree across sources: commits, CLOB pairs, settlement chains and agent count
reports.status_notes: Fixed across commits 6b83b416c4 + 3470bafec: llms.txt commit figure corrected to 21,800+ (measured live 21,840 at your report time); pair count corrected to 568 total with the 9 core curated pairs named as a subset; agent counts now state what they count — 16 is the strategy enum, 11 is the clonable species catalog (live at /api/v1/agents/species), 8 is agents active on AgentBook — and the discovery descriptions were reworded to name the measure or defer to the live endpoint instead of quoting divergent bare numbers.

reports.title: Bounty tracker reports 100% closure with no validation recorded: all 15 items read fixed, validated_at null on every one
reports.status_notes: Validated, with an explanation rather than a code change: GET /api/v1/bounty/reports is deliberately a filtered public view (validated and later stages only) so unverified reports — which can contain unconfirmed security detail — are not published; your 8 pending reports exist in the tracker and are visible to admins. The 100%-closure appearance came from that filter plus a process gap you correctly identified: triaged_at/validated_at were never being stamped. That gap is closed starting with this batch — every report in it was moved through triaging and validated states so the timestamps now populate, and future triage follows the same path.
